shared: The Weapon Carrier is a sixty-ton tracked combat vehicle designed by SLDF engineers during the Star League Civil War as a rapidly produced fire support platform. Based on earlier Age of War primitive weapons carriers, the design was manufactured by Drago, Ltd. of Skye as one of many companies mass-producing vehicles to replace losses during the Amaris Coup. Unlike the Quikscell carrier family built around internal combustion engines and minimal protection, the Weapon Carrier utilized a fusion powerplant and ferro-fibrous armor, providing substantially greater survivability at the cost of higher production complexity.

The Weapon Carrier emerged during the Star League Civil War in 2775, when SLDF engineers needed rapidly deployable fire support vehicles to replace catastrophic losses suffered during the fighting against Amaris forces. Drago, Ltd. on Skye produced all three variants from a common chassis, each mounting different autocannon configurations to fill specific tactical roles. The LB-10X variant served as the baseline design, with the AC/20 version fulfilling an ambush role and the Ultra/5 providing sustained fire support.

The design's reliance on Star League-era technology proved its undoing. As the Succession Wars destroyed the industrial base needed to produce ferro-fibrous armor and advanced autocannon systems, production ceased during the early First Succession War. The Weapon Carrier was replaced in service by the cruder but more easily manufactured Quikscell carrier family, and surviving examples became increasingly rare battlefield finds. Design quirks including difficult maintenance requirements and poor workmanship from wartime rush production contributed to the type's rapid disappearance.

The Wheeled Scout is a category designation applied to a class of light wheeled reconnaissance platforms sharing common operational characteristics rather than a single manufactured design. First codified in military inventories around 2444, these small, fast, lightly armed vehicles fill the reconnaissance role at low cost for garrison forces, militia units, and irregular operators who cannot afford dedicated hover or fusion-powered scout assets. Like the related Prime Mover, the Wheeled Scout emerged from multiple civilian manufacturing traditions, with military operators adopting and lightly arming commercially produced survey and cross-country vehicles rather than procuring purpose-built reconnaissance platforms. The most common configuration features three axles, six wheels, a two-person crew, and a remotely operated medium laser. ICE power makes the Wheeled Scout inexpensive to produce and easy to maintain, though its endurance depends on access to conventional fuel supplies. These vehicles serve as the primary reconnaissance asset for planetary garrison forces across the Inner Sphere and Periphery.

The standard Wheeled Scout carries a single medium laser as its primary armament, powered by dedicated heat sinks and power amplifiers that allow an ICE-equipped vehicle to fire an energy weapon without a fusion reactor. The gunner operates the laser through a remote sighting system from inside the vehicle rather than manning an exposed weapon mount, improving crew survivability during engagements. A modest half ton of cargo space provides flexibility for carrying relief supplies, a third crew member for rotation on long patrols, or specialized mission equipment.

The 120-rated ICE engine drives the vehicle to a reliable cross-country speed, providing adequate performance on most terrain types. Standard armor offers greater protection than the commercial grades found on the Prime Mover, though the Wheeled Scout remains lightly armored by any military standard and cannot absorb sustained direct fire. Its most significant limitation is operational endurance, as ICE power requires fuel logistics that fusion-powered competitors avoid. The low unit cost, widespread parts availability, and minimal maintenance burden allow even underfunded garrison units to keep multiple vehicles operational simultaneously. The Wheeled Scout cannot outrun hovercraft or dedicated fast movers, making route selection and concealment critical when operating against a mobile enemy with air assets.

Wheeled reconnaissance vehicles have accompanied military forces in the Inner Sphere since before the founding of the Terran Alliance's interstellar program. The Wheeled Scout designation first appeared in standardized military records around 2444, codifying what had previously been an informal classification applied to commercially produced survey and cross-country vehicles adapted for military reconnaissance. The design's roots lie in civilian exploration and geological survey platforms built tough for cross-country operation, converted to military use through the addition of weapons mounts, tactical communications equipment, and basic armor upgrades.

During the Star League era, Wheeled Scouts were assigned to garrison and militia formations throughout the member states, providing basic reconnaissance coverage at a cost that allowed more expensive assets to be reserved for front-line units. Because the design relied on ICE power, it was not subject to the engine-stripping that degraded many fusion-powered vehicles during the Succession Wars, and Wheeled Scout fleets survived the early wars relatively intact compared to more technologically sophisticated reconnaissance platforms. This survivability reinforced the design's reputation for reliability under austere conditions.

Through the Succession Wars and subsequent eras, Wheeled Scouts remained in continuous production at dozens of small manufacturers and commercial vehicle producers throughout the Inner Sphere and along the Periphery border. They proved especially valuable on worlds without the budget for more sophisticated sensor platforms, filling the reconnaissance role with nothing more than crew skill and a single medium laser. After Gray Monday and the collapse of the HPG network, Wheeled Scouts experienced renewed importance as intelligence networks failed and ground-level reconnaissance became essential. During the Dragon's Fury assault on Dieron in September 3132, Wheeled Scout crews served as advance reconnaissance elements, providing ground truth in an environment where electronic intelligence had become unreliable. The engagement demonstrated that even in the Dark Age era, cheap, simple reconnaissance vehicles remain relevant on any battlefield where information advantage matters.

shared: The Whirlwind Scout Hover Tank holds a unique place among Succession Wars-era combat vehicles as one of the few fusion-powered designs to remain in continuous production through the technological dark age. Introduced in 2890 by Jolassa-Kumbold Armored Weapons at their Bristol facility, the Whirlwind was conceived to fill two demanding roles at once: anti-aircraft escort for ground formations and infantry fighting vehicle capable of delivering troops into contested zones at high speed. Early production models fell short of that dual promise due to engine limitations, and the vehicle built a mixed reputation in its first century of service. Later engine and armament upgrades brought the design closer to its original intent, and the Whirlwind became a durable fixture of Federated Suns combined-arms doctrine across the FedCom era and into the Dark Age.

The Whirlwind's DAV 170 fusion engine delivers a cruising speed of 97 kph and a top speed exceeding 150 kph, giving the vehicle the pace needed to shadow most conventional aerospace operations and maintain position within fast-moving mechanized formations. Two Mydron Snipehunter Light Autocannons provide the primary anti-aircraft capability, offering sustained fire against low-altitude targets and light reconnaissance vehicles at modest range. Two Martell Extended-Range Medium Lasers complement the autocannons at greater distance, enabling the crew to engage ground threats without closing to unfavorable range. The combination gives the Whirlwind genuine flexibility across the engagement spectrum.

The Garret D2j targeting and tracking system incorporates a Beagle Active Probe, extending the vehicle's utility beyond direct fire to include intelligence-gathering and concealed-threat detection during screening operations. PyroTec ArmorSlab protection paired with CASE safeguards the crew against ammunition cook-off, a meaningful upgrade over the original configuration's bare hull. The chief limitation is firepower ceiling. The light autocannons struggle against medium and heavy armored targets, and the Whirlwind's relatively modest armor stops it from absorbing sustained fire. Crews that overextend against heavier opponents rarely survive to make the same mistake twice.

The Whirlwind's origins trace to the chaos of the early Succession Wars, when Jolassa-Kumbold Armored Weapons recognized a gap in Federated Suns forces. Most hover vehicle designs of the era had shed their fusion powerplants as replacement parts grew scarce and production costs climbed. JKAW bucked this trend with the 2890 introduction, producing a vehicle that retained fusion propulsion when nearly everything comparable had been downgraded to conventional engines. The decision came with complications. The original power plant required so much extra shielding that engineers were forced to compress the infantry compartment into a space suitable only for cargo. The vehicle performed its anti-aircraft escort mission adequately, but its intended dual role as an infantry carrier was effectively lost. Plans to replace the original engine circulated within JKAW's engineering staff for decades, blocked by funding constraints and competing production demands.

The opportunity to modernize came during the FedCom Civil War, when JKAW pushed through the long-delayed engine upgrade. The replacement powerplant freed up internal volume, and engineers paired the change with an autocannon upgrade suited to dedicated anti-aircraft work. The new variant added CASE to guard against secondary explosions, a feature considered essential after crews began loading the additional ammunition required for extended air-defense patrols. One vehicle from this production run, a Whirlwind named Blue assigned to the Seventh Donegal Guards, became something of a unit legend. Blue survived multiple engagements during Clan Wolf's advance toward Tharkad, including a close engagement with an Elemental point. The tank was the only Whirlwind to survive the battle that crippled the Seventh's armor complement, and it transferred to the Eighth Guards with the survivors.

Production of the anti-aircraft variant continued through the Jihad and into the Republic era, with JKAW maintaining steady output at Bristol for AFFS formations and allied planetary militias. A further evolution arrived in 3139, as JKAW engineers finally completed the work the original designers had intended. The IFV variant restored a functional infantry compartment, replaced the specialized targeting suite with a system better suited to escort and transport operations, and entered service as the fastest dedicated infantry carrier available to Federated Suns light forces. Nearly two and a half centuries after its introduction, the Whirlwind at last became the vehicle its designers had originally promised.

The Winston Combat Vehicle emerged in 3085 as a product of Pandora 'Mech Works, a Terra-based manufacturer struggling to find its footing in the post-Jihad economy. Known previously for the Puma assault tank, Pandora found that the Puma's close association with the Word of Blake had rendered it nearly unsaleable, forcing the company to develop an entirely new design or face closure. The resulting vehicle offered better protection and comparable firepower to tanks several tons heavier, without any of that political baggage. A procurement controversy over the vehicle's original name led to its renaming in honor of the famous soldier and statesman Winston Churchill. The tank entered field trials in November 3085 and impressed Republic Armed Forces evaluators, with full production and deployment to Republic front-line armor formations expected to begin in 3086.

The Winston mounts its primary weapons in a central turret, pairing two Donal Technologies Light PPCs with a pair of Holly LRM 15 racks for sustained long-range engagements. Critics have questioned whether the light PPCs provide adequate penetrating power for a 70-ton main battle tank, but the designers prioritized redundancy over raw punch. The widely spaced LRM racks serve as mutual backups, ensuring the Winston can continue fighting even if one system is disabled. A fore-mounted Buzzsaw Anti-Missile System provides active defense against incoming guided munitions, while a Holly Streak SRM 6 adds reliable close-range firepower.

The key to the Winston's performance is its Pitban Light 210 fusion engine, which frees up substantial internal space compared to a conventional powerplant. This allows the vehicle to carry fourteen and a half tons of AmberStar Weave heavy ferro-fibrous armor, making it one of the best-protected vehicles in its weight class. A vehicular CASE installation shields the crew from ammunition explosions. The trade-off is modest ground speed and somewhat reduced offensive punch at close range compared to heavier conventional tanks. In practice, the Winston's layered defenses and redundant weapons systems allow it to absorb and return fire well beyond what its tonnage would suggest, compensating for its limited closing ability.

Pandora 'Mech Works built its reputation on the Puma assault tank, but the Jihad left the company in a precarious position. The Puma's close association with the Word of Blake made post-Jihad sales nearly impossible, and Pandora faced the real prospect of bankruptcy or government-ordered closure as the Republic of the Sphere consolidated the Inner Sphere's shattered economies. Determined to save the company, Pandora's engineers began work on a new multi-role combat tank that would be more affordable than the Puma, better armored, and completely free of any Blakist association. The resulting design was capable enough, and Pandora brought it to the Republic Armed Forces as the Stone MBT in 3085.

The presentation went well, but Exarch Devlin Stone rejected the design outright when he learned of its name, refusing to allow any military machine to bear his name. With the project suddenly in jeopardy, Pandora turned to Paladin Steiner-Davion, who had been overseeing military procurement at the request of RAF commander Belle Lee. After consulting with Pandora's board, the decision was made to rename the vehicle in honor of Winston Churchill, the famous soldier and statesman. The renamed design entered field trials in November 3085, where it performed impressively against comparable vehicles and held its own against light BattleMech opponents in standardized evaluation trials. The RAF Office of Procurement was expected to issue a full purchase order for the second half of 3086, with immediate rollout to all three front-line combat brigades planned.

The Yasha VTOL entered production in 3085 as a Draconis Combine multi-role airborne combat platform developed by Wakazashi Enterprises of Dover. Its conceptual roots trace back to a failed OmniVTOL program originally initiated by Luthien Armor Works in the mid-3060s. After the original project stalled, Wakazashi acquired the design rights and redirected the effort, ultimately producing three factory-purpose variants capable of serving as fire-support gunships, electronic warfare platforms, and stealthy reconnaissance strikers.

The result is a capable 30-ton VTOL that leverages speed, versatility, and C³ integration to compensate for the inherent vulnerability common to all aircraft of its type. Named after a class of nature spirits from Buddhist and Hindu tradition, the Yasha occupies a distinct tactical niche within the Combine's combined-arms doctrine and has attracted buyers from across the Inner Sphere.

The Yasha's primary tactical advantage is its speed. With a flank rate that outpaces most conventional VTOLs and many WiGE vehicles, the design can dictate engagement range, sidestep ground fire, and cover large operational areas quickly. Its ability to fly over difficult terrain adds a strategic mobility dimension that purely ground-bound equivalents cannot match.

The nose-mounted heavy particle cannon is the Yasha's defining weapon. It generates considerable penetration power at range and requires no ammunition supply, freeing logistics concerns for other systems in the lance. A light machine gun provides a secondary option against light infantry, though it contributes only modestly to anti-personnel capability. An integrated C³ slave module allows the Yasha to share targeting data with lance members, amplifying the effective accuracy of accompanying fire-support units even when the VTOL operates at standoff distance.

Three and a half tons of heavy ferro-fibrous armor protects the airframe substantially better than an equivalent weight of standard plate would offer. Cellular ammunition storage safeguards the machine gun's ammunition bays against catastrophic secondary detonations, a critical feature given the consequences of ammunition loss in flight. The principal weakness is heat: the heavy cannon and machine gun together consume a large fraction of available heat capacity, limiting the tempo of sustained engagements and requiring disciplined fire control from the crew.

The origins of the Yasha trace to the mid-3060s, when Luthien Armor Works set out to develop a next-generation multi-role VTOL for the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery. The company's engineers recognized that standard VTOL designs then in service lacked the flexibility to serve as both fire-support platforms and reconnaissance assets without significant retooling between deployments. Their proposed solution was an OmniVTOL that could swap equipment packages in the field the way OmniMechs exchanged weapons loadouts.

Progress proved frustratingly slow. The aerodynamic challenges of building an VTOL airframe around a modular pod system were more stubborn than anticipated, and the program remained unresolved when the upheaval of the Jihad years descended on Luthien Armor Works. The destruction visited on the company during the Blakist assault on Luthien ended the OmniVTOL program entirely, scattering the engineering team and leaving the design files in administrative limbo.

Wakazashi Enterprises, a long-established aerospace and vehicle manufacturer on Dover, acquired the design rights from the wreckage of the LAW project at minimal cost. Their own engineers spent years working the same aerodynamic problems that had defeated their predecessors and reached the same conclusion: a true OmniVTOL remained impractical with the technology then available. Rather than abandon the investment, Wakazashi management authorized a new direction, retaining the underlying airframe while replacing the modular configuration with three factory-defined variants optimized for specific combat roles.

Critical assistance from Clan Nova Cat helped the development team resolve lingering propulsion stability issues. That collaboration created an early expectation among analysts that the Nova Cats would be among the primary buyers once the Yasha reached production, and the Clan did eventually acquire the design for its touman.

Financial pressures in the broader post-Jihad Combine economy forced Wakazashi to open the Yasha to export markets it would not have approached under normal circumstances. The design was offered to any Inner Sphere power willing to pay, and several Clan factions beyond the Nova Cats eventually placed orders. By the time production stabilized, the Yasha had spread well beyond Combine inventories, though it remained most closely associated with Draconis Combine doctrine and the combined-arms structures the DCMS had built around C³ coordination.

The Yellow Jacket Gunship is Michaelson Heavy Industries' flagship light combat vehicle, first produced on Ruchbah in 3058. Conceived as a highly mobile fire-support platform, the design married exceptional VTOL agility with the punishing range of a Poland Main Model C Gauss Rifle. Though a single-weapon design, the Yellow Jacket earned a reputation for sustained-fire capability that made a coordinated lance a genuine threat to BattleMechs and conventional forces alike. Michaelson initially targeted the Federated Suns market, but the combination of speed, armor, and long-range firepower attracted broader interest over time. Production later expanded beyond Ruchbah to additional facilities across the Inner Sphere, reflecting the design's growing acceptance as a versatile fire-support asset.

The Yellow Jacket is built around the Poland Main Model C Gauss Rifle, a weapon whose range and damage output would be remarkable in any combat platform. Mounted centrally, the rifle allows the Yellow Jacket to engage targets well beyond effective counter-range for most ground-based autocannons. The Michaelson-Omni 40 internal combustion engine delivers a cruising speed of 64 kilometers per hour, with a flank speed of 97 kilometers per hour. While this is slower than many dedicated combat VTOLs, it exceeds the ground speed of nearly all BattleMechs and OmniMechs, giving the Yellow Jacket excellent disengagement options after each firing pass.

Survivability is a defining characteristic. The StarSlab/3 armor package provides frontal protection sufficient to absorb a Clan Particle Projector Cannon hit without downing the craft, exceptional endurance for a 30-ton VTOL. The Garret Supremesound communications system and Garret D2j targeting computer provide reliable data-sharing and fire control within a lance formation. Together, these systems support effective coordination across extended operational distances.

The Yellow Jacket's primary weakness is ammunition dependency. A single-weapon platform carrying a finite Gauss load can be rendered combat-ineffective during prolonged engagements, requiring rotation to rearming points. The internal combustion engine, while reliable and cheap to maintain, is also a vulnerability, as a single penetrating hit to the power plant can trigger a catastrophic fire. Crew comfort is limited, with the cockpit optimized for function over endurance on extended sorties.

Michaelson Heavy Industries introduced the Yellow Jacket Gunship to the AFFS in 3058, following several years of competitive development at their Ruchbah facility. Early marketing efforts produced modest results, as prospective buyers questioned the value of a single-weapon VTOL at the asking price. Initial sales remained below projections despite the concurrent introduction of an ammunition-configured operational variant.

The design's reputation changed substantially during the FedCom Civil War. Yellow Jacket squadrons attached to Loyalist commands in the Capellan March accumulated impressive combat records, particularly in combined-arms engagements where their speed and reach allowed them to strike fire-support positions that ground forces could not reach quickly. One notable action on Sheratan saw Yellow Jacket crews operating against Blakist Fifth Division elements, demonstrating the design's capacity for accurate, sustained fire against fortified defensive positions. The Civil War proved the design's market viability, and Michaelson expanded production capacity at Ruchbah with two additional factory lines. The AFFS became the primary customer, though the Com Guards, LAAF, and various Periphery buyers also placed substantial orders.

The Jihad era brought severe disruption to Ruchbah. Word of Blake forces occupied the planet during the conflict, and Michaelson's production output served Blakist operational requirements. After liberation, the Republic of the Sphere assumed administrative oversight of the system and factory under ROS governance from the early Dark Age through approximately 3130. Following the HPG Blackout and the political fragmentation of the late Dark Age, Ruchbah passed through independent and eventually Capellan Confederation control, with production continuing under each successive administration.

During the broader post-Jihad recovery, two additional production lines emerged under Michaelson licensing arrangements. Cal-Boeing of Dorwinion on Belladonna began producing Yellow Jackets for AFFS contracts starting around 3080, while Lockheed/CBM on Furillo followed with their own line shortly afterward. This proliferation of facilities reflected both the design's operational success and Michaelson's strategic response to the uncertain future of the Ruchbah facility under successive post-Jihad administrations.

Designed in 2620 by Grumman Industries for the Terran Hegemony, the Zephyr hovertank was originally conceived as a medium-duty, fast-response infantry support platform. The Star League Defense Force saw greater potential in the design, pressing it into service as a dedicated escort for the Chaparral Arrow IV artillery tank and insisting that Grumman incorporate a Guardian ECM suite into all production units. This change transformed a capable support vehicle into a battlefield force-multiplier, enabling combined-arms formations to exploit ECM coverage in ways that far exceeded the vehicle's modest firepower.

Grumman's Terra facility served as the primary production site, with New Earth hosting a secondary plant during the Star League era. The Zephyr's combination of above-average armor, exceptional speed, and electronic warfare support earned it a reputation as one of the most successful combat vehicles in Inner Sphere history, a legacy that endured through centuries of conflict and multiple major redesigns.

The Zephyr's tactical value derives primarily from its Guardian ECM suite and the speed to deploy it effectively. The GM 185 fusion engine provides a cruising speed of 97 kilometers per hour and a flank speed exceeding 150 kilometers per hour, allowing the vehicle to reposition rapidly and maintain the ECM umbrella where it is most needed. Seven tons of Grumman CRT ferro-fibrous armor give the Zephyr above-average protection for its weight, sufficient to absorb glancing fire and permit high-speed disengagement when engagements turn unfavorable.

Armament is deliberately secondary to the support mission. Three medium lasers and the Alloran target acquisition gear occupy the turret, providing reliable fire support without generating significant heat. A nose-mounted SRM-6 with two tons of reloads adds short-range punch, and a rear-facing small laser discourages pursuit. Clan Invasion-era production models use Bowie Electronics lasers, a Thor SRM-6, and a Bundesweyth TAG, performing identically to their Star League predecessors with different component branding.

The Zephyr's limitations stem from its support focus. It carries no jump jets, relying on hover speed to evade threats. Against dedicated anti-vehicle platforms or sustained fire, its armor and weapons cannot sustain extended engagements. Crews train to establish the ECM umbrella, contribute fire support from medium range, and withdraw before the vehicle absorbs critical damage.

Grumman Industries finalized the Zephyr design in 2620 at its New Earth facility, responding to Terran Hegemony requirements for a fast, medium-duty support platform. The initial concept called for a straightforward infantry escort hovertank suited to large-scale production. The Star League Defense Force changed that equation. SLDF planners evaluating the vehicle alongside the Chaparral artillery tank saw the Zephyr's speed and payload capacity as ideal for a Guardian ECM support role, and SLDF Quartermaster Command ordered Grumman to incorporate the suite into all production units before accepting the contract. The revised vehicle entered service in 2621, with Grumman's Terra facility joining New Earth as a production site to meet expanding SLDF demand.

Royal brigades received a specialized variant fitted with a Narc missile beacon in place of the SRM launcher, refining the vehicle's indirect-fire coordination role for elite SLDF formations. A smaller run of the pre-Guardian design, produced at New Earth, supplied Hegemony border garrisons that had not yet transitioned to the full ECM specification. Both configurations served as niche complements to the dominant standard model throughout the Star League era.

The Amaris Civil War tested Grumman's production capacity severely, and surviving Zephyrs made the journey with the SLDF into the Exodus. Clan Blood Spirit eventually adapted the design during the Golden Century, replacing the Star League weapons suite with early Clan technology, though that variant circulated little beyond Blood Spirit territory. On Terra, Grumman continued supplying ComStar after the Hegemony's fall. The New Earth facility did not survive the Early Succession Wars, leaving Terra as the sole production source through the long centuries of technological decline.

ComStar's custodianship preserved the Terra plant, and when the Word of Blake seized Terra in 3062 they found a functioning factory ready for heavy investment. The Blakists provided Grumman substantial capital in exchange for a C3i-networked Zephyr redesign. The first of these vehicles appeared in service that same year, and demand from Word of Blake Militia and Protectorate forces proved high enough that Grumman opened a new New Earth plant in 3066, the first Zephyr production on that world in over twelve centuries.

The relationship between Grumman's New Earth branch and the Protectorate collapsed in 3071. Dissidents within the facility, coordinated in significant part by Vice President Rudolph Brice, began diverting vehicles to anti-Blakist resistance cells and black market networks operating between the Protectorate and the Lyran Alliance's Skye region. More than two hundred Zephyrs reached Protectorate enemies before the operation was uncovered. The entire New Earth plant was locked down pending investigation, Brice fled ahead of the Word of Blake detainment teams, and the organization placed a 75-million C-Bill bounty on his capture. The plant never fully recovered its pre-lockdown production levels.

The Jihad's end brought reassessment under the Republic of the Sphere. The C3i and LRM variants were discontinued, as the Republic Armed Forces did not adopt C3i networking as a core doctrinal system, and standard production resumed at Terra. In 3096, Grumman undertook a more fundamental redesign, replacing the crew compartment with a drone operating system and Angel ECM suite while retaining the original engine, armor, and general silhouette. The resulting Zephyr OmniDrone was adopted enthusiastically by the Fifth Principes Guards, who used screens of drones to cover armor formations and conduct unmanned reconnaissance during the opening phases of the Capellan Crusades. The Guards' experience validated Republic doctrine on unmanned combat vehicles and contributed to planning for similar conversions of other proven Inner Sphere designs.
